🏥 NAMO Hospitals — What We Did
PART 1 — Created the Hospital Website
Step 1: Created the website files

We created the basic website using:

index.html → website structure
styles.css → website design
script.js → website functionality

The website contains things like:

Home
About
Doctors
Services
Contact
Login
Patient Details
Appointments




PART 2 —
 Created DynamoDB Database

Step 2: Created a DynamoDB table In AWS DynamoDB, we created:

Table name:
paticienttable_namo_hospitals

Step 3: Created the Primary Key

We used:
Partition key: patient.id
and:
Sort key:admission_date

So one patient's database record looks roughly like:

patient.id       → P001
admission_date   → 2026-09-24
name             → Ravi
age              → 35
doctor           → Dr. Niketa Sonavane

PART 3 — Created Lambda


Step 4: Created Lambda function

We created: hospital-api

Runtime: Python 3.14

Architecture: x86_64

The Lambda's job is to communicate between our website and DynamoDB.

The basic flow is:

Website
   ↓
Lambda
   ↓
DynamoDB



PART 4 
— Gave Lambda Permission


Step 5: Created IAM permission

Lambda needs permission to access DynamoDB.

We gave the Lambda role permission for:

PutItem
Scan on:

paticienttable_namo_hospitals

So:

Lambda
   ↓
Permission
   ↓
DynamoDB



PART 5 — Wrote Lambda Code


Step 6: Added GET functionality

We made Lambda understand:

GET

GET means:

"Give me the patient data."

It uses:

table.scan()

So:

Website
   ↓ GET
API Gateway
   ↓
Lambda
   ↓
DynamoDB
   ↓
Patient data


Step 7: Added POST functionality

We also made Lambda understand:

POST

POST means:

"Save this new patient data."

It uses:

table.put_item(Item=body)

So:

Website
   ↓ POST patient data
API Gateway
   ↓
Lambda
   ↓
DynamoDB
   ↓
Saved


PART 6 — Tested Lambda

Step 8: Tested GET

We tested Lambda with:

{
  "httpMethod": "GET"
}

It successfully retrieved patient records.

Step 9: Tested POST

We tested Lambda with patient information.

For example:

P999
Test Patient
9999999999
Dr. Rahul Sharma
10:30

Lambda returned:

Patient added successfully

And we checked DynamoDB.

The patient was there. ✅

This proved that Lambda → DynamoDB was working.

PART 7 — Created API Gateway

Step 10: Created HTTP API

We created:

namo-hospitals-api

API Gateway gives our website a public API address.

Our API endpoint is:

https://v3zad59huh.execute-api.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com
PART 8 — Created API Routes
Step 11: Created GET route

We created:

GET /patients

which connects to:

hospital-api



Step 12: Created POST route

We created:

POST /patients

which also connects to:

hospital-api

So our complete backend became:

                    ┌──────────────┐
                    │   Website    │
                    └──────┬───────┘
                           │
                    POST /patients
                           │
                           ▼
                    ┌──────────────┐
                    │ API Gateway  │
                    └──────┬───────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                    ┌──────────────┐
                    │    Lambda    │
                    └──────┬───────┘
                           │
                           ▼
                    ┌──────────────┐
                    │   DynamoDB   │
                    └──────────────┘



PART 9 — Configured CORS

Step 13: Enabled CORS

Because our website is running separately from AWS, the browser needs permission to communicate with the API.

We configured:

Allow Origin:
*

Methods:

GET
POST

Header:

Content-Type

This allows our localhost website to communicate with API Gateway.



PART 10 — Connected Website to API

Step 14: Modified script.js

Previously, the appointment form was only showing:

Appointment Confirmed

It wasn't actually saving anything.

We changed it so the website sends data to:

/patients

using:

fetch(...)

The website creates data like:

const patientData = {
    "patient.id": patientId,
    "admission_date": date,
    "name": first + ' ' + surname,
    "phone": phone,
    "doctor": doctor,
    "appointment_time": time
};

Then:

fetch(API_URL, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(patientData)
});
PART 11 — Fixed the JavaScript Error
Step 15: Changed function to async

Because we used:

await fetch(...)

we needed:

async function

instead of:

function

So:

appointmentForm.addEventListener('submit', async function (event) {

This is important because await only works inside an async function.



PART 12 — Fixed Localhost

Step 16: Started a local web server

Initially you were opening:

file:///home/suman-manyam/namohospitalswebsite/index.html

That caused browser security problems.

So we started a local server:

cd /home/suman-manyamam/namohospitalswebsite
python3 -m http.server 8000

Small correction: your actual folder is:

/home/suman-manyam/namohospitalswebsite

So use:

cd /home/suman-manyam/namohospitalswebsite
python3 -m http.server 8000

Then we open:

http://localhost:8000

🧠 Easy way to remember the whole project

Think of it like a hospital reception:

Website = Patient fills the form 📝
API Gateway = Reception desk 📋
Lambda = Hospital staff processing the form 👨‍💻
DynamoDB = Hospital database 🗄️

So:

Patient fills form → Reception receives it → Staff processes it → Database stores it.
